subject: Comparing replacement vendors: licensing cliffs, onboarding credit & support handoff
messages:
From: Danielle Park <dpark@astride.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor replacement — economics and support handoff

Jordan,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We're starting an internal evaluation to replace our current inference vendor and I wanted to outline the main commercial asks up front so Procurement and the CTO org can compare apples to apples. High level:

- Current incumbent is offering 25% off list for year 1 + a $150k migration credit, but they also require a 24 mo minimum commitment and have a license cliff if we terminate early.
- Our concerns are: (1) true onboarding / professional services effort (ops handoff, KV cache migration, pre-warming), (2) support SLA & escalation path, and (3) short-term cash impact if we commit longer than the first year.

Can Redwood provide a comparable two-part structure (onboarding credit + commitment discount) and also clarify how you handle the operational transfer (handbook/runbook, on-call coverage during cutover, and rollback credits if migration stalls)? If you can share a brief cost delta / TCO for us to present to Procurement that breaks out the migration uplift vs. unit-cost savings, that would be ideal.

I attached our migration planning workbook for context.

Looking for a quick sketch this week — Rajeev (CTO) and Procurement will review.

Thanks,
Danielle Park
Head of Platform Programs
Astride.ai

Attachments: Astride_Migration_Workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@astride.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor replacement — economics and support handoff

Danielle —

Appreciate the context and the workbook. I pulled together a short delta TCO and an initial commercial pattern that maps to the incumbent's ask but with more explicit operational safeguards. See the attached "redwood-delta-tco.pdf" for the line items. Summary below:

1) Two-part offer (example numbers; open to refinement):
   - Onboarding credit: $120k applied to first 90 days (covers runbook creation, KV migration assistance, testing windows, and up to 5 days of on-call engineering during cutover).
   - Commitment discount: 18% off list in year 1 if you commit to 12 months; 22% off for a 24-month commit. Credits are applied before the commitment discount.

2) License cliff handling: we propose a pro-rata refund of unused committed usage for early termination during the first 6 months, plus a reduced break fee after month 6 (details to be captured in the SOW). This is intended to mitigate the incumbent-style cliff.

3) Support handoff and escalation: we include a 30-day runbook transfer period where our solutions engineer pairs with your ops team, and a 2-week on-call overlap during final cutover. For larger migrations we can add a guaranteed 48-hour SLA for P1 for the first 60 days.

4) Operational transfer: to align expectations we suggest a short pilot (3–5 days of production-like runs) to validate KV cache warming and latency targets; any extra eng time beyond the onboarding credit would be biled at an agreed hourly rate or applied to an uplift bucket.

If that approach looks acceptable at a high level, can we schedule a 30-min walkthrough with Rajeev and Procurement to line up acceptance criteria and any regulatory/controls evidence (SOC 2, data residency)? I can also convert this into a draft amendment + SOW for legal review.

-Jordan

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-delta-tco.pdf (summary PDF)

Quick note from AE side —

I like the two-part structure Jordan suggested. A couple of pragmatic tweaks from deals desk that have helped close similar accounts:

- Make the onboarding credit refundable only if we miss agreed milestones (keeps customers engaged and limits open-ended liability).
- Add a rollback credit schedule (e.g., 50% of onboarding credit if migration reversed within 30 days) so Procurement sees a true cost-of-failure number.
- Put a 90-day QA milestone for performance (latency p50/p95) that gates the full release of the onboarding credit.

I can draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) to include the milestones, acceptance criteria, and who signs off.

- Laura

Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@astride.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor replacement — economics and support handoff

Danielle — attaching a short risk matrix and my recommended migration sequence. High-level technical notes:

- Migration lift: the dominant cost is KV prefix transfer and cache warm; for your 20M daily tokens workload we expect ~3–4 engineer-days for automation + up to 5 days for pre-warm runs if you want <50ms p95 parity during launch. That fits inside the onboarding credit estimate above if we keep scope to the core models.

- Support handoff: we'll provide a runbook + playbook and shadow your on-call for 10 business days around cutover. If you require fortnightly runbook updates post-cutover, we should reflect that in the SOW (time-and-materials or add-on retainer).

- Data/residency & SOC2: from a technical control perspective SOC2 evidence is standard; share the exact artifact list Procurement needs and we can produce it within 48–72 hours.

- License cliff: incumbents often front-load discounts and then apply heavy termination fees. Operationally, that creates friction. Our suggested economic compromise: smaller onboarding credit (vs. their $150k) but more flexible early-exit protection (pro-rata refunds + defined break fee tiers). That reduces immediate cash pressure and gives you an escape path if performance isn't met.

I'm attaching migration-risk-matrix.csv with estimated hours per task.

-Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Director, Applied ML & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Attachments: migration-risk-matrix.csv (CSV)

From: Danielle Park <dpark@astride.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor replacement — economics and support handoff

Jordan / Karthik / Laura —

This is helpful, thanks. Procurement and Rajeev reviewed the sketch and we have two asks before we can move to a formal amendment:

1) We need SOC2 Type II evidence and a list of control mappings for our security review (required before DocuSign). You mentioned 48–72 hours — pls send the artifact list and the report or a link to the secure bucket.
2) Add an explicit rollback credit schedule into the amendment: if we have to revert within 30 days, Astride receives 50% of the onboarding credit back; within days 31–90, 25%. That needs to be codified.

If you can send the formal amendment + SOW with those two items and a DocuSign link, Procurement will review and aim to turn the amendment in 3–5 business days. We prefer a 12-month commit with the onboarding credit applied up-front.

Thanks — if you can cc legal@astride.ai on the amendment, that will speed approval.

Danielle

Danielle Park
Head of Platform Programs
Astride.ai
